messages:
ana: Kicking off canary for model v2.3-int8 (quantized NVL) to 2% traffic. Please watch MRR, rerank precision, and latency tails. Starting now.

deploy-bot: canary start: model=v2.3-int8 percent=2 policy=staged duration=30m 

matt: thanks — listing the quick checks: overall MRR, long-doc recall slice, rerank P@1, 95p latency tail, token-per-response cost.
jordan: add hallucination rate on the small-sample eval set (sampled 5k chats). If that moves, we should be conservative.
lee: grabbing baseline numbers (from last 24h shadow of v2.2): MRR=0.784, rerank_P1=0.912, halluc_rate=0.012, latency_95=420ms.

ana: typo — "ana" meant. baseline uploaded to /mnt/evals/baselines/v2.2-canary.json 

matt: quick proposal for automatic fallback thresholds: if any of the following hold within the canary window, trigger auto-fallback to v2.2: 
- MRR drop <= -1.2% (relative) AND p-value < 0.05 on bootstrap
- rerank P@1 drop <= -0.8% absolute
- hallucination rate increase >= +0.6 percentage points
- latency_95 increase >= +120ms absolute

jordan: +1 to that. Also require at least 5000 matched sample events OR 1% of total traffic -> prevents noisy early stops.
lee: running short AB locally on current slice — initial signal: MRR delta = -1.6% (rk_mean -0.0126), p=0.03, samples=6,200. Rerank P@1 delta = -0.3% (within noise).

matt: that's crossing the MRR threshold. Can we check cohort breakdown? Might be concentrated on long-docs or system-prompt heavy flows.
jordan: pulling slice breakdown: long-docs (seqlen>2k) delta MRR = -3.2%; short queries delta = -0.1%. Looks concentrated.

ana: ops question — do we prefer an immediate rollback or a staged throttle (pause ramp)? Suggest: pause further ramp from 2% to 10% and roll back at 2% -> safer and fast.
lee: agree. Operational runbook says: if major metric crosses threshold on important slice, pause and rollback at current percent.
matt: I'll trigger a manual pause and request rollback if deploy-bot won't auto-fallback yet. @deploy-bot can you hold ramp?

deploy-bot: action: ramp_hold applied for model=v2.3-int8 at 2% by matt. Next check in 5m.

jordan: can we also enable kv-warmup on a small fraction of long-doc traffic and re-run? The quantization may be cold-kv sensitive.
nana: good point — enable kv-warmup flag for 0.5% traffic to long-doc slice: config snippet:
```
route: long-doc
model_override: v2.3-int8
flags: { kv_warmup: true }
percent: 0.5
```

lee: spun up warmup slice. Re-run AB on that slice only. Early metrics in 10m.
matt: note for postmortem: we should add a pre-onboard long-doc stress test for quant variants (simulate kv-warm sequences).
jordan: +1. Also logging suggestion: emit per-request kv_cache_hits and softmax_temp stats to aid root cause.

deploy-bot: monitor report (10m): overall MRR delta = -1.4% p=0.04; long-doc MRR delta = -2.9%; warmup-slice delta = -0.5% (statistically noisy).

ana: conclusion: auto thresholds triggered for MRR but concentrated on long-docs and improved slightly with kv_warmup. Action plan: 
1) Rollback to v2.2 at 2% traffic (manual) to stop user impact.
2) Create a follow-up job: reproduce long-doc regression in local cluster with kv cache instrumentation.
3) Run a targeted optimization pass (kv-cache order, attention chunking) and re-run canary with pre-warm policy.

matt: I'll handle rollback and open a ticket: ML-ONBOARD-421: "v2.3-int8 long-doc regression - investigate kv heatmap and attention chunking".
lee: I'll seed a synthetic long-doc burn-in harness and attach logs.
jordan: let's update our canary template to require long-doc smoke for quant variants before visible ramp. Saves future cycles.
nana: thanks all. Rolling back now. @deploy-bot confirm when rollback is complete.

deploy-bot: rollback: model=v2.3-int8 -> v2.2 at 2024-08-19T15:40:30Z by matt. canary stopped. event_id=rbk-1719004321-1 :thumbsup:

matt: rollback confirmed. I'll ping again once we have repro and a mitigation PR.

ana: nice fast reaction. filing postmortem doc and adding checklist item: "quant canary: long-doc smoke required". :memo:
